raw_text:
Here is a structured 12-week “couch-to-5K” plan tailored for a 24-year-old male with exercise-induced asthma (well-controlled on SABA), aiming to complete a 5K in 12 weeks. It emphasizes gradual progression, proper warm-ups, asthma-friendly guidelines, and injury/recovery. It includes weekly structure, sessions, exercises, sets/reps (or time), and nutrition/recovery notes. Adjust as needed for individual tolerance and medical advice.

Assumptions and safety notes
- Warm-up: Begin every session with a 5–10 minute, low-intensity warm-up (dynamic mobility and brisk walking). End with a 5-minute cool-down and gentle stretches.
- Asthma management: SABA as prescribed. If symptoms occur (cough, chest tightness, wheeze, shortness of breath), stop, use rescue inhaler per plan, and resume only when symptoms resolve and you’re ready. Do not push through significant symptoms.
- Environment: Prefer warm, humid or temperate conditions; avoid cold-air, high-intensity work in cold without a plan. If outdoor cold air is unavoidable, incorporate a longer warm-up, scarf/face covering, and reduce intensity.
- Medical clearance: If any new or worsening symptoms occur, consult clinician before continuing.
- General guidelines: 1–2 rest days per week. Strength and mobility work on non-running days help reduce injury risk and asthma triggers. Hydration and adequate sleep support performance.

Week-by-week progression overview
- Weeks 1–3: Run-walk intervals to establish baseline tolerance, focusing on form, breath control, and consistent habit.
- Weeks 4–6: Increase running exposure with longer continuous intervals and reduced walking time.
- Weeks 7–9: Build sustained running blocks, introduce gentle pace progression and mild hills if accessible.
- Weeks 10–12: Peak long run and consolidation, mimic 5K pace in final sessions, taper and race rehearsal.

Detailed plan

Weeks 1–3: Foundation and habit
Goal: establish routine, lowest sustainable running effort, emphasize breathing technique and proper warm-up.

Week 1
- Session A (3 days this week): Run-walk mix
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes brisk walk; dynamic movements (leg swings, hip circles, arm circles).
  - Workout: 20 minutes total time
    - 1 minute easy jog
    - 2 minutes walk
    - 1 minute easy jog
    - 2 minutes walk
    - 1 minute easy jog
    - 2 minutes walk
    - 1 minute easy jog
    - 2 minutes walk
  - Cool-down: 5 minutes slow walk; 5 minutes gentle stretching (quads, hamstrings, calves, chest).
  - Focus: maintain easy breathing, relaxed shoulders, light cadence. Use nasal or mouth breathing as comfortable; avoid hyperventilation.

- Session B (2 days this week): Strength + mobility
  - Full-body circuit 2 rounds:
    - Bodyweight squats: 12 reps
    - Push-ups (knees or full): 8–12 reps
    - Glute bridges: 12 reps
    - Dumbbell or resistance band rows: 12 reps
    - Step-ups: 10 reps per leg
    - Plank: 20–30 seconds
  - Mobility: hip flexor/hamstring stretches, thoracic spine mobility
  - Optional: light 5–10 minute bike or elliptical if available for cardio cross-training.

Week 2
- Session A: Run-walk mix, slightly longer overall time
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes
  - Workout: 22 minutes total
    - 1 min jog
    - 2 min walk
    - 1 min jog
    - 2 min walk
    - 1 min jog
    - 2 min walk
    - 2 min jog
    - 2 min walk
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes; light stretching
  - Focus: comfortable pace, keep breath under control.

- Session B: Strength + mobility (same circuit, add 1 more round if tolerable)
  - 2–3 rounds of the same circuit
  - Add 1–2 new mobility drills: thoracic rotations, ankle dorsiflexion mobility

- Optional Session C (if energy allows): Easy cross-training
  - 20–25 minutes of cycling or swimming at easy effort; keep it conversational.

Week 3
- Session A: Run-walk progression
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes
  - Workout: 24–26 minutes total
    - 2 minutes jog
    - 2 minutes walk
    - 2 minutes jog
    - 2 minutes walk
    - 2 minutes jog
    - 2 minutes walk
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes, stretches
- Session B: Strength + mobility
  - Lower volume but add a bit more load if comfortable:
    - Goblet squats or dumbbell squats: 3 sets of 10
    - Dumbbell rows: 3x10
    - Hip thrusts: 3x12
    - Plank: 3x30 seconds
  - Mobility: hip flexor, calf, thoracic spine
- Optional C: Easy run 15 minutes total, continuous or with 1–2 short walking breaks.

Phase transition reminder after Week 3: If running intervals are well-tolerated with minimal asthma symptoms, you can begin to reduce walking portions more over the next phase. If any symptoms persist, slow progression and consider an extra week at the current volume.

Weeks 4–6: Build running time and reduce walking
Goal: Increase continuous running time and maintain quality form while managing asthma triggers.

Week 4
- Session A: Run-walk with longer running blocks
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes
  - Workout: 28–30 minutes total
    - 3 minutes jog
    - 2 minutes walk
    - 3 minutes jog
    - 2 minutes walk
    - 3 minutes jog
    - 3 minutes walk
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes
- Session B: Strength + mobility
  - Lower body focus plus core:
    - Lunges: 2×10 per leg
    - Dumbbell deadlifts: 3×12
    - Push-ups: 3×10–12
    - Side planks: 2×20 seconds per side
  - Mobility: ankle and hip work
- Optional C: 20–25 minutes easy cross-training

Week 5
- Session A: Longer continuous running window
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes
  - Workout: 30–32 minutes total
    - 5 minutes jog
    - 2 minutes walk
    - 5 minutes jog
    - 2 minutes walk
    - 5 minutes jog
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes
- Session B: Strength + mobility
  - Add resistance: chair-assisted push-ups, goblet squat, single-leg Romanian deadlift with light dumbbell
  - Core work: dead bug or bird dog 3×10 per side
- Optional C: Easy 20–25 minute swim or bike

Week 6
- Session A: Mostly continuous with brief walk break as needed
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes
  - Workout: 34–36 minutes total
    - 8 minutes jog
    - 2 minutes walk (if needed)
    - 8 minutes jog
    - 2 minutes walk (if needed)
    - 6–8 minutes jog to finish
  - Goal: reduce walking frequency; permit one short walk break if form holds and asthma stable
- Session B: Strength + mobility
  - Emphasize posterior chain and core
  - Superset: glute bridges 3×12, rows 3×12
  - Core: side planks 2×25 seconds per side
- Optional C: 25 minutes easy tempo cycling or brisk walk

Weeks 7–9: Endurance and pace confidence
Goal: Build longer continuous runs; introduce mild pace awareness and asthma-friendly pacing.

Week 7
- Session A: Continuous run focus
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes
  - Workout: 28–32 minutes continuous running, aim for a conversational pace
  - If fatigue or breathing becomes challenging, insert a 1–2 minute walk break as needed
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes
- Session B: Strength + mobility
  - Full-body routine with modest progression:
    - Split squats: 3×10
    - Dumbbell chest press or push-ups: 3×10–12
    - Dumbbell rows: 3×12
    - Pallof press or anti-rotational core: 2–3×8 per side
  - Mobility: hip flexor, thoracic spine
- Optional C: 20–30 minutes low-intensity cardio (bike/swim)

Week 8
- Session A: Progressive run
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes
  - Workout: 30–34 minutes continuous
  - Include some gentle strides: 3 efforts of 20–30 seconds at a comfortably hard pace, but not all-out
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes
- Session B: Strength + mobility
  - Maintain form; integrate single-leg work (step-downs, pistol progression to chair)
  - Core: dead bug variations
- Optional C: Active recovery: mobility flow or light swim

Week 9
- Session A: Longer steady run
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes
  - Workout: 34–38 minutes continuous
  - Focus on consistent pace; avoid surges
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes
- Session B: Strength + mobility
  - Maintain volume; 2–3 sets of 10–12 reps for major movements
- Optional C: Easy cross-training 20–30 minutes

Weeks 10–12: Peak and race preparation
Goal: Simulate 5K duration and pacing, refine breathing, taper toward race week.

Week 10
- Session A: 5K-pace practice blocks
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes
  - Workout: 32–40 minutes
    - 4 minutes jog
    - 2 minutes walk
    - 4 minutes jog
    - 2 minutes walk
    - 4 minutes jog
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes
  - If you can, perform one 10–12 minute continuous run at a comfortable pace within this window.
- Session B: Strength + mobility
  - Maintain functional strength with moderate loads
  - Core circuit: 3 rounds
- Optional C: Easy 20–30 minutes

Week 11
- Session A: Taper-friendly longer run
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes
  - Workout: 28–36 minutes easy-to-moderate pace; include one 5-minute continuous block if comfortable
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes
- Session B: Strength + mobility
  - Focus on maintaining strength; keep intensity moderate
- Optional C: Light cross-training 20–25 minutes

Week 12: Race week and taper
Goal: Fresh legs, confidence, and race readiness.

- Session A: Shorter run with strides
  - Warm-up: 5–10 minutes
  - Workout: 20–25 minutes total
    - 6 minutes jog
    - 6×20–30 seconds at a brisk, controlled pace with 1 minute easy jog between (strides)
    - 5 minutes easy jog
  - Cool-down: 5–7 minutes
- Session B: Light strength and mobility
  - 2 sets of 8–10 reps for major moves; low volume
- Optional C: Rest or very light activity (walk, gentle mobility)

Race week suggestions
- Plan your last hard session 4–5 days before the 5K, with easy running and strides on the days prior.
- Ensure adequate hydration and carbohydrate intake to support training and race-day energy.
- Sleep 7–9 hours per night; manage stress and exposure to asthma triggers (pollution, cold air, allergens).

Run-specific nutrition and recovery
- Pre-run: 30–60 minutes before easy runs, a small snack if needed (banana, yogurt, toast with light jam). For longer sessions, consider a small carb source 60–90 minutes prior.
- Hydration: Aim for consistent hydration throughout the day; drink water regularly. For longer sessions, a sports drink can help replace electrolytes.
- Post-run: Within 30–60 minutes, have a balance of carbs and protein (e.g., chocolate milk, yogurt with fruit, or a protein shake with a small carb source). This supports recovery and reduces airway symptoms due to post-exercise inflammation.
- Asthma triggers: If environmental triggers are present (dust, cold air, high pollen), consider indoor sessions or postponing outdoor workouts on high-risk days. Use inhaler as prescribed if symptoms arise.

Strength and mobility components
- Frequency: 2 days per week during weeks 1–9; 1–2 days per week during weeks 10–12, as the running volume increases and race approaches.
- Core and mobility: Include core work (planks, side planks, pallof presses) and mobility (hip flexor, ankle dorsiflexion, thoracic spine) in every week.
- Progression: Increase resistance or reps gradually every 2–3 weeks if techniques remain solid and symptoms are controlled.

Pacing and breathing tips
- Maintain a conversational pace; if you cannot hold a conversation, slow down.
- Practice nasal breathing or pursed-lip breathing if helpful, but prioritize comfortable breathing patterns that avoid over-tightening the chest.
- If chest tightness or wheeze occurs, stop, use rescue inhaler as prescribed, and resume only when symptoms subside and you’re comfortable.

Progression summary
- Weeks 1–3: Run-walk intervals focusing on habit formation.
- Weeks 4–6: Increase run time, shorten walking breaks.
- Weeks 7–9: Emphasize longer continuous runs with occasional pace strides.
- Weeks 10–12: Practice race-equivalent effort and pacing; taper toward the 5K.

If you want, I can tailor specific daily sessions into a printable 12-week calendar with exact days of the week, per-session cues, and a simple tracking sheet for distances, pace, and asthma symptoms. Also, I can adjust the volume if the client has constraints (time, equipment) or if the therapist prefers more or fewer strength sessions.
